record.summary: Data center campus planned by ACS with Benbros Energy on about 25.5 hectares of industrial land in La Puebla de Alfindén, Zaragoza province. Announced in June 2025 with EUR 1,254 million for the first phase and 150 MW of grid access at Red Eléctrica's Peñaflor substation; a second phase depends on a further 150 MW the developers have requested. The regional plan describes two data halls of 40 MW and 60 MW of IT load, a new 400/220 kV substation next to Peñaflor and an underground line to the site. The plan won initial approval in December 2025 and was amended in July 2026 to add the power line projects. Urbanisation works were expected from late 2026 or in 2027.

record.summary: TOK1 is AirTrunk's flagship hyperscale campus in the Inzai data center hub east of Tokyo, which AirTrunk bills as the biggest hyperscale campus in Japan measured in megawatts. The 13-hectare campus is scalable to more than 300 MW and already has facilities in service. In August 2024 AirTrunk said a 50 MW third phase was on schedule and topping out; it broke ground on a further 40 MW-plus phase in June 2025, and in March 2026 said it had recently begun building over 100 MW of additional IT load. That month it closed a JPY 191.6 billion green loan to refinance existing TOK1 facilities and fund the next phases.

On 28 January 2026 the Aragón government declared it an investment of regional and general interest, citing EUR 3.9 billion in total: EUR 1.125 billion for a first phase due in 2029 and EUR 2.775 billion for later phases. record.summary: Proposed off-grid AI data centre park in the Greenview Industrial Gateway south of Grande Prairie, Alberta, announced in December 2024 by O'Leary Ventures with the Municipal District of Greenview and now led by O'Leary Digital. Backers describe up to 7.5 GW of on-site gas and geothermal generation built in phases, starting with 1.4 GW. O'Leary Digital said in February 2026 that Alberta permitting was underway; a December 2025 report said the site was undeveloped and construction might not start until late 2028. Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation lost an appeal of the gateway's water licence in April 2026; in August 2026 a judge refused an O'Leary-backed bid to halt a Nation challenge.

record.summary: Second xAI supercomputer campus, in a building of about one million square feet on Tulane Road in the Whitehaven area of Memphis, near the Mississippi line, which xAI bought in 2025. The site has drawn little or no grid power and runs mainly on gas turbines at a former Duke Energy plant site about 1.5 miles away in Southaven, Mississippi. Mississippi regulators permitted 41 permanent turbines there in March 2026, and environmental and civil rights groups appealed the permit in April 2026. Analyst estimates put its IT load near 1 GW by mid-2026. Anthropic says it has GPU capacity here under an agreement with SpaceX.

record.summary: AI supercomputer that xAI built in 2024 inside the former Electrolux manufacturing plant on Paul R. Lowry Road in southwest Memphis. Grid power comes from MLGW and TVA through an existing MLGW substation and a new one paid for by xAI, supplemented by permitted on-site gas turbines and battery storage. Anthropic now describes Colossus 1 as SpaceX's data center, and in May 2026 it agreed to use all of the site's compute capacity, stated as more than 300 MW and over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs.

record.summary: Third xAI data center in the Memphis area, made by retrofitting a warehouse of roughly 800,000 square feet that xAI bought in late 2025 in Southaven, Mississippi, just south of Colossus 2 across the state line. Mississippi's governor announced it in January 2026 as an investment of more than $20 billion, the largest economic development project in state history, supported by a state sales and use tax exemption and local fee-in-lieu agreements. Musk said it would lift Colossus training compute to about 2 GW, and a July 2026 report relaying his comments said it holds 220,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs.

record.summary: YTL Power International is developing a large data center park in Kulai, Johor, paired with a solar plant of about 500 MW and backup supply from the national grid. The park was first described as a 500 MW campus; GDS agreed in 2022 to co-develop part of it, and YTL announced an AI infrastructure collaboration with Nvidia in December 2023. YTL said in late 2025 that an Nvidia GB200-based AI data center at the park was operational, with about 300 MW being built and commissioned. In August 2026 it was reported to be bringing capacity online progressively and planning to raise the park's ceiling from 600 MW to 1,000 MW.
